explanations: The loop calls res.write for every user and ignores its return value. When the client reads slowly, write() returns false but the handler keeps pulling 500-row pages from Postgres as fast as the database allows, so the whole export accumulates in the response's in-memory write buffer. For a tenant with millions of users this can exhaust process memory. It should await the 'drain' event when write() returns false (or pipe a Readable built from the generator).
Each query uses WHERE u.id > $2 ORDER BY u.id LIMIT $3 and sets afterId to the last row's id. There is no OFFSET, no DECLARE CURSOR (each page is a separate pool query), and no full load.

req.on('close') flips aborted; the loop checks it each iteration and breaks, which also finalizes the generator so no further pages are queried, and res.end() is skipped. It doesn't drain the remaining pages, doesn't throw, and has no retry.

Headers and the first two pages are already written, so the status can't change; the catch logs and calls res.destroy, cutting the stream. A 500 body is impossible after headers are sent, the export doesn't continue past the error, and 401 only applies before streaming.
